one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall in the window. (1) GEV Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-28, before the open (IR events page). The CEO said at Morgan Stanley's Laguna conference (2026-09-16) that he expects 'a very strong third quarter orders performance', that the 20 GW second-half gas commitment outlook is 'likely conservative', and that 2032 slots are already selling with cash committed; consensus Q3 EBITDA is about $1.7B. The read-across from the chain is positive: Siemens Energy booked 15 GW in its June quarter and raised its market view to 110-120 GW a year, Caterpillar power generation sales rose 72%, and Eaton's US data-center backlog is 307 GW. But the stock has already bounced about 13% from the $874 close on 2026-09-14, so a good print is partly priced; the stock has moved 5-15% on recent results. (2) Hyperscaler Q3 results in the last week of October (MSFT, GOOGL, META, AMZN). September guidance showed no cuts at any of seven spenders, and Alphabet has guided 2027 capex up 'significantly'. The tail risk is any capex softening after the 2026-09-14 AI-lab slowdown calls. Texas's data-center interconnection audit (since 2026-08-03) is a slow-moving overhang, not a dated event. Net: median about $1,000 (+1.3%, a slight positive tilt for the orders signal), log-sd about 16% (52%/3.5 plus some extra for earnings), close to symmetric.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion: after the 2026-09 slowdown calls, hyperscaler 2027-28 plans get cut or pushed out (they now spend about 100% of cloud revenue on capex, with external financing rising). Behind-the-meter projects get cancelled (the Crusoe-Boom cancellation is a template), Texas's audit holds back 50 GW of load, and slot reservations (63 of 116 GW) convert slowly or lapse. Siemens, MHI, Doosan and Baker Hughes capacity arrives into a 2030-31 glut, as GLJ argues. About 25x on about $24 EPS, and Wind losses persist.

base.story: Gas reaches more than 125 GW under contract by YE26, the $200B backlog comes in early 2027, and 2030-32 slots sell at premium pricing (Siemens and MHI confirm three-year-plus lead times and favorable pricing). Electrification grows 25%+ against a 307 GW US data-center backlog (Eaton) and transformer shortages, and Wind is near breakeven. 2028E EPS of about $32.5 at about 33x.

bull.story: Hyperscaler capex reaches $1.3-1.45T in 2027 (S&P Global, UBS), PJM shortfalls (6.8 GW short, with an uncapped price of $555/MW-day) and grid-connection limits push more utility and behind-the-meter gas orders, and $/kW keeps stepping up. Margins beat the 20% 2028 framework, EPS reaches about $37, and the stock trades at about 41x.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $640 (35% under today and well below the post-selloff low of $874), the market would be pricing a real drop in gas-turbine order intake or reservation cancellations, not just a lower multiple: the GLJ cyclical case (2030-31 overcapacity) playing out early, or hyperscaler capex being cut structurally. Either breaks the industry-wide sold-out-through-2030 thesis that Siemens Energy, MHI and GEV all describe.

reasoning: Industry lane, continuation run with about 28 additional searches and fetches. The value chain still strongly supports GEV's demand case, and the new evidence adds to it. Customers: all seven large capex spenders raised or held 2026 guidance in the September round with no cuts (Supercycle HQ), Alphabet guides 2027 up 'significantly', and S&P Global projects six hyperscalers at $1.3T of 2027 capex, about 50% higher. Competitors: Siemens Energy raised its gas market view to 110-120 GW a year with pricing 'favorable', and its grid backlog is a record EUR 51B; MHI has 35 GW and capacity doubling; Caterpillar power generation sales are up 72% with a $72B backlog and orders out to 2030; Bloom revenue is up 166%; Wartsila orders are up 33%; Eaton's US data-center backlog is 307 GW. Regulators: PJM's 2028/29 auction cleared at the cap and 6.8 GW short (uncapped price $555). Costs: IEEFA documents new combined-cycle cost at about $2,000-2,500/kW, which supports GEV pricing. GEV itself: the CEO says Q3 orders will be very strong, 2H commitments of 20 GW are conservative, and 2032 slots are selling. Bear evidence I could not chase before: GLJ's quantified 2030-31 overcapacity case (104-113 GW of capacity vs 88-90 GW of orders); new supply from Doosan (12 US units) and Baker Hughes (2.7 GW a quarter); Crusoe cancelling a 1.2 GW Boom turbine order; Texas pausing data-center interconnections (49.8 GW at risk, BNEF); and documented project delays, although SemiAnalysis shows the 'half of 2026 cancelled' story is overstated. Verified facts: 266.3M shares at 2026-06-30 (270M diluted in Q2), and 2026 GAAP EPS inflated by a $4.0B Prolec gain. Consensus 2027/2028 EPS is about $24.9/$30.5-34.8, and 2027 FCF is about $7.4B. Valuation: fair value about $1,040 (P/E, FCF yield and EV/EBITDA), about 5% above spot; the median target is $1,250. Distribution: a mixture of a base lognormal (median $1,100, sigma 0.38, weight 0.82) and an 18% bear component (median $640, sigma 0.32) for an AI-capex air pocket or a cycle turn. That gives 52% at or above spot and a fatter left tail than a plain 52%-vol lognormal. Changes from the capped run are small, because the new evidence cut both ways.
